requirements.PJE-CFG-001: The default settings carry a per-domain column mapping for all six domains (EX, AE, LB, CM, MH, DS) plus the identity, time, window, lane and filter configuration; every column is overridable.
requirements.PJE-CFG-002: The plan's camelCase setting spellings (`contextWindowDays`, `onAnchorEvent`, `sourceUrlTemplate`, lane-level `severityCol`/`seriousCol`/`tests`) are accepted as aliases and normalized onto the canonical snake_case keys; the canonical key wins when both are given.
requirements.PJE-CFG-003: `lanes` merges key by key so a partial override back-fills; a lane set to null is disabled; an unknown lane key is dropped with a console warning.
requirements.PJE-CFG-004: `context_window_days` is coerced to a non-negative integer, defaulting to 30; zero is a legal window meaning the anchor day only.
requirements.PJE-DATA-001: `init` accepts either a merged array carrying a domain column or an object of per-domain arrays, with domain keys and domain values matched case-insensitively; both forms normalize to the same internal model.
requirements.PJE-DATA-002: A merged-array row whose domain value is missing or unrecognized is dropped with a named reason rather than being assigned to a default domain.
requirements.PJE-DATA-003: Rows that cannot be used are dropped with a per-domain named reason, counted by domain and reason on the instance, reported in the notes, and exportable as CSV led by the reason column — nothing is dropped silently.
requirements.PJE-DATA-004: Required columns are validated per supplied domain against the data contract, and every missing dataset column is named in one error whose message renders into the target element.
requirements.PJE-DATA-005: An absent domain is not an error: its lanes render an explanatory empty state and their toggles are disabled, so a partial journey still draws.
requirements.PJE-DATA-006: The raw row objects passed to `init` are retained by reference and never mutated; every derived value lives on the module's own normalized record.
requirements.PJE-DATA-007: Each day column setting accepts an ordered fallback chain resolved per row, so both the analysis-day and the domain-day vocabularies place a record, and the column that resolved it is recorded on the event.
requirements.PJE-DATA-008: A record whose end day precedes its start day is kept, drawn as a single-day mark, and counted in a named flag rather than being silently converted into an open-ended record.
requirements.PJE-SUBJ-001: The subject selector lists every participant present in any domain, sorted, and opens on the first (or on the configured `subject`).
requirements.PJE-SUBJ-002: A search box filters the subject list case-insensitively by substring; selecting a subject redraws every lane, clears any anchor, and announces the new subject.
requirements.PJE-SUBJ-003: `selectSubject(id)` selects programmatically; an unknown id changes nothing and warns.
requirements.PJE-LANE-001: One lane renders per enabled domain in the fixed order exposure, dose changes, adverse events, labs, con-meds, medical history, disposition, each with a permanent text label in the left gutter.
requirements.PJE-LANE-002: A lane toggle hides and shows its lane without changing the shared day domain, so the other lanes do not move.
requirements.PJE-LANE-003: Lanes are grouped into collapsible groups with `aria-expanded` disclosure buttons; collapsing a group hides its lanes and keeps the axis fixed.
requirements.PJE-LANE-004: Every lane chart shares one x-axis minimum and maximum and one pinned y-axis width, so the lanes align by construction rather than by measurement.
requirements.PJE-LANE-005: The labs lane renders one small-multiple sparkline per configured test on the shared day axis, with the reference range drawn as a band and out-of-range points marked by shape as well as colour.
requirements.PJE-LANE-006: Exposure bars segment at each dose change, and each change carries a direction glyph (increase, reduction, interruption, restart) rather than being encoded by colour.
requirements.PJE-LANE-007: A subject with no adverse events renders the adverse-event lane with an explanatory note rather than removing the lane or failing.
requirements.PJE-LANE-008: Records with no usable study day are kept and named in prose beneath their lane rather than dropped, so absence of a day is visible.
requirements.PJE-LANE-009: The opening participant's enabled lanes fit the configured panel height without vertical scrolling: heights scale down to their floors first, and when even the floors do not fit the panel scrolls and says so rather than cropping.
requirements.PJE-LANE-010: A lane whose rows exceed the row cap draws a deterministic subset in the lane's documented sort order and names both the remainder and the sort rule in prose, and the anchor panel reconciles its counts against what was drawn.
requirements.PJE-DERIV-001: Dose changes are derived from consecutive exposure records per subject, ordered by start day, classified as increase, reduction, interruption or restart, and dated to the day the new dose begins.
requirements.PJE-DERIV-002: A lab test's baseline is the record flagged as the analysis baseline when the data carries that flag, falling back to the last value on or before the configured baseline day and then to the earliest recorded value, with the rule that fired recorded on the result.
requirements.PJE-ANCH-001: Activating any placeable mark anchors time on it: the axis **relabels** to days from the anchor, the anchor reference line is drawn on every lane, and `anchor(null)` clears it. Anchoring never re-ranges or zooms the shared day domain — the whole journey stays visible.
requirements.PJE-ANCH-002: The context window is the anchor plus and minus the configured elapsed days, inclusive; interval records match by overlap and point records by containment, and a record with no end day matches as still running while carrying whether its end is recorded as ongoing or simply not recorded.
requirements.PJE-ANCH-003: Marks inside the window are drawn at full strength inside a highlighted band; marks outside it are de-emphasized while keeping their hit target, tooltip, tab order and full-strength listing in the source drawer.
requirements.PJE-ANCH-004: The anchored axis is an offset count labelled "Days from anchor": the anchor is day 0 and the scale is linear across it, deliberately unlike CDISC study-day numbering, and the guide states the difference.
requirements.PJE-ANCH-005: All window and offset arithmetic runs in a continuous elapsed-day space with no day 0, so a window of N days spans N elapsed days on each side of the anchor and "days from anchor" equals the calendar difference between the two dates for every pair of days, including pairs that straddle first dose.
requirements.PJE-ANCH-006: A notice above the lane stack says that clicking any mark shows the events associated with it and names the keyboard path; once a mark is anchored the notice says which mark is anchored and how to move or release the anchor; with every lane off, or before data is bound, the notice is not shown.
requirements.PJE-CTX-001: Con-meds active at the anchor are those starting on or before the anchor day and not ending before it; a con-med with no usable start day is not asserted to be active and is counted as not evaluated, and a con-med whose end was never recorded is counted as active but separately counted and named as such in the panel rather than asserted to have continued.
requirements.PJE-CTX-002: Abnormal labs in the window are those whose normal-range indicator is present and not normal, or whose value is at least twice or at most half the baseline, with the triggering reason recorded.
requirements.PJE-CTX-003: Dose changes falling inside the window are listed with their direction and the day the new dose began.
requirements.PJE-CTX-004: Earlier or same-day adverse events with the anchor's preferred term (falling back to the verbatim term) are listed most recent first, over the whole record rather than only the window — unchanged by any display filter or lane toggle — with each row stating its offset from the anchor and a same-day record saying so.
requirements.PJE-PANEL-001: The side panel lists the four context kinds with counts, an explicit empty state per kind, the not-evaluated counters, and a standing sentence that co-occurrence is not causation.
requirements.PJE-SRC-001: Every mark and every panel item links back to its source row by a real control, not only by a named id: the drawer shows the raw object as supplied under a stable anchor id, and both the mark's own open-source control and a panel item scroll that row into view and focus it.
requirements.PJE-SRC-002: When `source_url_template` is configured each source row carries an external link built from the row's own values; with no template configured no link is rendered.
requirements.PJE-FILT-001: The serious-only filter restricts the adverse-event lane to serious events and leaves the other lanes untouched.
requirements.PJE-FILT-002: The abnormal-labs-only filter restricts lab points to those failing the abnormality rule.
requirements.PJE-FILT-003: The con-med class filter is a multiselect over the recorded classes, with uncoded records kept as their own selectable bucket rather than hidden.
requirements.PJE-FILT-004: A filter whose column is absent from its domain's data is dropped with the library's standard console warning.
requirements.PJE-TIME-001: The display switches between study day and calendar date, relabelling ticks, tooltips and panel text while the underlying scale stays linear in days.
requirements.PJE-TIME-002: Study day maps to calendar date from the subject's reference date with day 1 as that date and no day 0.
requirements.PJE-TIME-003: A partial recorded date (year, or year and month) is shown as recorded and never used to position a mark.
requirements.PJE-TIME-004: When a record's full recorded date disagrees with its study day, the study day positions and labels the mark, the disagreement is named in the tooltip, and the affected records are counted in the notes.
requirements.PJE-EVT-001: Subject selection, anchoring and context changes are delivered three ways — settings callbacks, instance listeners and a DOM CustomEvent on the shell root — carrying the whole context bundle, so a consumer never reads the DOM.
requirements.PJE-EVT-002: Selecting a subject also dispatches the library's shared `participantsSelected` event carrying that subject.
requirements.PJE-EVT-003: `off` removes listeners and `destroy` tears down charts, listeners and the container; the instance is not reusable afterwards.
requirements.PJE-KEY-001: Every drawn mark is a real focusable control with an accessible name naming its domain, label, days and flags; one mark per lane is in the tab order and a visible two-ring focus indicator is drawn.
requirements.PJE-KEY-002: Enter or Space on a focused mark anchors time on it and re-activating clears it; Escape clears the anchor.
requirements.PJE-KEY-003: Arrow keys move chronologically within a lane and to the nearest mark in the adjacent lane, and a polite live region announces the subject, the anchor and the context counts.
requirements.PJE-KEY-004: Focus is restored onto the recreated control after any rebuild, so filtering or toggling a lane does not drop the keyboard user to the top of the page.
requirements.PJE-ACC-001: The mark palette passes the documented validator at the hardest pairlist in both modes: three categorical hues whose **composited** fills — as drawn, at full strength and at the de-emphasized strength — measure at least 3:1 and between 1.9:1 and 2.4:1 against their surface respectively, with worst CVD separation ΔE 13.0; lane identity beyond three lanes is carried by position, a permanent label and mark geometry, never hue.
requirements.PJE-ACC-002: No encoding is carried by colour alone: severity varies bar height and border weight at a single opaque fill, an unrecorded severity draws a distinct hatched mark named in its accessible name, seriousness adds a filled start dot and an SAE tag, lab direction is a glyph, and dose direction is a caret shape.
requirements.PJE-ACC-003: Module text meets AA at its rendered size: every text node the module renders measures at least 4.5:1 against its computed background in the browser, and the library's `#7b8b96` muted ink, which measures 3.51:1, appears nowhere in the module's source.
requirements.PJE-DEMO-001: The vendored demo extracts are reproducible and guarded: the exposure extract keeps only dosing records, the con-med extract is de-duplicated to one row per distinct course, the medical-history day is the collection day, and the subject count and seeded subjects' key values are asserted.
requirements.PJE-DEMO-002: The built demo page mounts against the vendored extracts with no console errors and opens on the seeded subject.
requirements.PJE-DEMO-003: Against the vendored CDISC Pilot 01 extracts, anchoring the seeded participant's day-30 adverse event produces the panel counts the guide documents, with each item linking back to its source row — the Definition of Done, executed.
requirements.PJE-NARR-001: The five narrative skills (event-context, subject-summary, lab-trajectory, dose-journey, disposition) and the three shared documents (system prompt, style guide, refusal catalog) compile from the skills folder into one module: each skill carries its slug, a semantic version, its grounding tool and its declared tool list in front matter, and `Input`, `Draft` and `Output` definitions in its schema. The committed compile is the catalog a fresh compile of the folder produces, so an edit to a prompt that was never rebuilt fails the suite rather than shipping silently.
requirements.PJE-NARR-002: The six read-only tools — `get_subject_overview`, `get_events`, `get_context_window`, `get_lab_series`, `get_dose_history`, `get_source_row` — return structured rows and never prose, and every row carries a `row_id` that is the chart's own event id. `get_context_window` returns exactly the context bundle the panel renders, row for row, and every failure (unknown subject, unresolvable anchor, unknown test, row or tool name) comes back as an `{ error }` object rather than throwing.
requirements.PJE-NARR-003: A generation runs the skill's declared grounding tool first, before any model call, and hashes the result: `input_hash` is a SHA-256 over the canonical JSON of the skill slug, its version, the run inputs and the grounding rows. The draft cache is keyed by `skill@version`, that hash and the adapter, so the same rows under the same skill and provider are never generated twice.
requirements.PJE-NARR-004: The tool loop admits only the tools the skill declares — any other name is returned to the model as a `tool-not-available` error — and is capped at a configured number of tool calls per generation beyond the grounding call, after which the model is told to submit. Every row id returned by any tool in the generation joins that generation's citation scope.
requirements.PJE-NARR-005: The validator runs on every model submission, in order: the skill's `Draft` schema, then citation resolution against the rows the tools returned in this generation, then the style guide's forbidden constructs, then the sentence cap. A sentence whose citations do not all resolve is dropped and recorded in `provenance.dropped`; a schema failure or a forbidden construct is a hard failure; a sentence over the cap is dropped with its reason; and `status` is `draft` on everything the validator returns.
requirements.PJE-NARR-006: A failed validation is retried exactly once with the errors fed back to the model, and a second failure becomes a `refused:validation` draft. Empty grounding refuses as `refused:insufficient-data` with no model call at all; an adapter throw, a provider refusal stop reason and an aborted signal map to `refused:provider-error`, `refused:provider-refusal` and `refused:cancelled`; and every refusal is a schema-valid draft with no sentences, exactly one `refused:<reason>` flag and complete provenance.
requirements.PJE-NARR-007: Every draft, refusals included, carries complete provenance: the model, `skill@version`, the `input_hash`, the generation timestamp, the ordered list of tool calls with the grounding call first, the adapter name, token usage, the number of submission attempts, and every dropped sentence with the reason it was dropped.
requirements.PJE-NARR-008: One adapter interface — `messages({ system, messages, tools, model })` returning content blocks, a stop reason, usage and the model — carries every provider: Claude over the Messages API by raw HTTP with `apiKey` or `getToken` and an overridable `baseUrl`, sending an effort setting rather than a temperature on the current models, which reject temperature; OpenAI over Chat Completions behind the same interface; and a deterministic offline stub whose drafts are templated from the real grounding rows, so every citation resolves and every number is the chart's own.
requirements.PJE-NARR-009: The `narratives` setting is a block of five slot functions, one per skill, kept only when the value is a function; a slot with nothing bound requests nothing and renders nothing, so the mechanical chart is unchanged. With `subjectSummary` bound, the participant summary renders above the lane stack as a light-blue card labelled "AI narrative" showing a one-line blurb that expands to the full cited draft.
requirements.PJE-NARR-010: Anchoring an event drafts its context card at the top of the context panel's body, above the con-med section, and every sentence in it is prefixed with a `Draft — AI generated` chip. A refusal renders the refusal catalog's text for its reason as the card's summary rather than an empty card or a blank space.
requirements.PJE-NARR-011: A citation chip is a real control: activating it lights the cited mark on the timeline and moves keyboard focus to it, Escape clears the highlight, and a cited row that is not drawn — its lane off, a filter, the row cap — opens its source record instead and announces that it did.
requirements.PJE-NARR-012: Staleness is recomputed on every render from the same grounding scope hash the generation runtime uses: a change to the context window re-requests the event narrative and emits a regenerate action, and a filter that changes the grounding rows greys the card, says the rows moved and offers Regenerate rather than discarding the draft.
requirements.PJE-NARR-013: Accept, Reject, Edit and Regenerate emit `{ type, kind, subject, row_id, draft, editedSentences?, reason? }` on all three channels — the `on_narrative_action` settings callback, `on()` instance listeners and a `pjeNarrativeAction` DOM event. The chart never marks anything accepted itself: the host decides and passes the draft back through `refreshNarrative(draft)`, and a draft returned with `status: 'accepted'` flips the card's chips.
requirements.PJE-NARR-014: Lab, dose and disposition narratives are not drafted automatically: each is requested from a control in a tray beneath the axis strip — one per drawn lab test, one for the dose journey when exposure rows exist, one for disposition when its rows exist — and its card renders in that tray, outside the lane stack so the stack's height budget is untouched. Selecting a different participant drops every narrative card, so a draft is never shown against another participant's record.
requirements.PJE-NARR-015: The evaluation harness scores a golden set of at least 30 cases across the five skills, built from the vendored CDISC Pilot 01 extracts, with rule-based graders — faithfulness, coverage, hallucination, style and refusal correctness — and an optional LLM-as-judge second opinion, against thresholds recorded per skill. `npm run eval:narratives` writes a report, and the stub-adapter run under the rules grader is a CI gate.
requirements.PJE-NARR-016: The demo page carries an "AI narratives" section that binds the offline stub adapter by default, so the published site builds and deploys with no secret and every visitor sees working, fully cited drafts. A toggle switches to Claude with a visitor-supplied API key that is kept in that browser tab only and sent directly from the browser to the API, never to the site's host.
requirements.PJE-NARR-017: The style guide's forbidden-phrase block rejects causal, diagnostic, treatment, prognostic and re-identifying language while accepting the guide's hedging vocabulary unchanged, and the runtime's own SHA-256 implementation reproduces known digests.
